checks.q: A manager uses experience to apply a sales report. Which DIKW level is this?
checks.teach: Applying information using understanding is knowledge. Wisdom is the judgment used to choose a sensible action after considering the situation.

checks.q: Which IS component is the cashier who uses the checkout system?
checks.teach: The cashier is a human participant. The steps they follow are the process; the app they use is software.

checks.q: Which hardware holds active work temporarily?
checks.teach: RAM is temporary working space. The CPU executes instructions; persistent storage keeps saved files.

checks.q: A business charges a recurring fee for continued access. Which model?
checks.teach: Recurring access fees characterize subscriptions. A marketplace connects buyers and sellers; a franchise licenses a business approach.

checks.q: A seller bundles equipment with installation and training. Which slide example fits?
checks.teach: The seller adds services to another company’s product, creating a more useful bundle.

checks.q: In DSRP, comparing a customer’s and an employee’s views uses which pattern?
checks.teach: Perspectives are viewpoints. Different people can experience the same process differently.

checks.q: In DSRP, asking what belongs inside a system and what larger whole it belongs to uses which pattern?
checks.teach: Systems thinking includes nested parts and wholes. Distinctions instead identify what something is and is not.

checks.q: In DSRP, asking how stock shortages affect delivery uses which pattern?
checks.teach: You are examining how one thing affects another: a relationship.

checks.q: Which process model shows the proposed improved workflow?
checks.teach: To-be describes intended future work. As-is captures how the work currently happens.

checks.q: Which detail belongs in a process model?
checks.correct: Who performs an activity and which decision determines the next step
distractors: Only employee job titles without workflow
checks.teach: A useful process model describes work, actors, decisions, and sequence so handoffs and problems become visible.
checks.answer: Who performs an activity and which decision determines the next step

checks.q: A salon performs a customer’s haircut. Which core process is this work?
checks.teach: Production includes creating a service. It is not limited to making factory goods.

checks.q: A bakery identifies a flour shortage and sends an order to a supplier. Which process?
checks.teach: The bakery is buying resources it needs. From the supplier’s side, supplying that order is fulfillment.

checks.q: Which is a sensible output of the accounting process?
checks.teach: Accounting takes financial events as inputs, checks and organizes them, and produces records and reports.

checks.q: Which output belongs to procurement?
distractors: Only a finished product made from raw materials
checks.teach: Procurement gets resources into the organization. Production later transforms those resources.

checks.q: Which input most directly starts fulfillment?
checks.teach: Fulfillment follows a customer’s request through preparation, delivery, and payment.

checks.q: An employee asks the purchasing department to buy a monitor. Which document is this?
checks.teach: The request is still internal. The organization later sends a purchase order to the selected seller.

checks.q: The seller sends a bill. What is it called from the buyer’s perspective?
checks.teach: The buyer receives a request to pay its vendor. The same bill is a sales invoice from the seller’s perspective.

checks.q: A process gets faster but doubles its error rate. What should you conclude?
checks.correct: Evaluate speed and quality together against the goal
distractors: It is definitely better because time fell
It is definitely more effective because errors rose
Ignore quality when evaluating a process
checks.teach: Improvement must serve the intended outcome. Fast incorrect orders may not satisfy the goal.
checks.answer: Evaluate speed and quality together against the goal

checks.q: Removing one duplicate approval from the existing workflow is usually what?
checks.teach: It is a small adjustment to the current workflow rather than fundamental redesign.

checks.q: Replacing the entire order-handling approach with a new cross-functional design is what?
checks.teach: The basic design and responsibilities are being reconsidered. That is the radical scope of re-engineering.

checks.q: Is an EA framework the same thing as the company’s architecture?
checks.correct: No; the framework structures the work, while architecture is the company’s design
distractors: Yes; both mean the installed hardware
Yes; both mean only the database
No; architecture means goals only and a framework means profits
checks.teach: A framework supplies ways to describe and develop a design. The resulting architecture is specific to the enterprise.
checks.answer: No; the framework structures the work, while architecture is the company’s design

checks.q: Defining customer and order records belongs most directly to which architecture layer?
checks.teach: Data architecture concerns the structure and management of data assets, including these records.

checks.q: Defining how ordering and inventory apps interact belongs to which layer?
checks.teach: Application architecture describes applications and their interactions in support of business work.

checks.q: Defining the company’s fulfillment process and decision responsibilities belongs to which layer?
checks.teach: Business architecture covers processes, organization, strategy, and governance.

checks.q: Defining required servers, supporting software, and networks belongs to which layer?
checks.teach: Technology architecture describes the capabilities needed to run applications and data services.

checks.q: Must SOA services be hosted in the cloud?
checks.correct: No; reusable services can run on premises or in the cloud
distractors: Yes; any locally hosted service stops being SOA
Yes; SOA simply means any website
checks.teach: SOA describes software organization around services. Hosting location is a separate choice; the slide uses a simplified cloud association.
checks.answer: No; reusable services can run on premises or in the cloud

checks.q: Two branches use the same order form but never share records. What is present?
distractors: Neither, because all forms must be different
checks.teach: The form is consistent, but work and records are not connected between the branches.

checks.q: A new sale automatically updates inventory and accounting. What does this illustrate?
checks.teach: The transaction connects several business functions so each can act on shared information.

checks.q: Does “single version of the truth” mean an ERP automatically fixes wrong data?
checks.correct: No; shared records still require accurate inputs and controls
distractors: Yes; shared storage guarantees all facts are correct
Yes; only separate databases can contain errors
No; ERP prevents all departments from viewing records
checks.teach: Shared data reduces conflicting copies, but a wrong value can still be shared widely. Data quality remains essential.
checks.answer: No; shared records still require accurate inputs and controls

checks.q: Moving old records into ERP is called what?
checks.teach: Migration is the transfer of data into the new environment, where formats and accuracy need checking.

checks.q: A supplier accesses a buyer’s purchasing process online. Which ERP II feature does this show?
checks.teach: The work crosses company boundaries, extending the internal integration emphasized by ERP I.

sorts.teach: Facts become meaningful information, then usable understanding, then informed judgment.

sorts.q: Translate strategy into a working system
sorts.teach: First decide the goal, then required business behavior, then the design, then concrete technology.

items: Select vendor and send purchase order
sorts.teach: In this simplified flow, know the need before ordering and inspect delivery before paying. Contract payment timing can vary.
The customer’s order starts the flow. This example bills after delivery; other businesses collect payment earlier.
Work is designed, used, checked, and improved. The cycle then continues.
This simplified path assumes enough stock. A full activity diagram also shows the no-stock branch.

cloze.q: Raw facts are ____; organized facts with meaning are ____.
cloze.teach: Data are the starting facts. Processing or contextualizing them produces information.

cloze.q: DSRP’s ____ asks about viewpoints; ____ asks about interactions.
cloze.teach: A viewpoint is a perspective. How things affect each other is a relationship.

cloze.q: An internal purchase request is a ____; the order sent to the vendor is a ____.
cloze.teach: Internal approval happens inside the buyer. Ordering from a selected supplier goes outside the organization.

cloze.q: For efficiency, compare planned ____ with actual ____.
cloze.teach: Efficiency in slide 20 is PI/AI: both values concern resource use.

cloze.q: For effectiveness, divide ____ output by ____ output.
cloze.teach: The achieved result is compared with the initial output target.
The amount produced per resource unit is productivity, such as orders per hour.

cloze.q: Small changes to an existing process are ____; fundamental redesign is ____.
cloze.teach: Improvement preserves much of the process. Re-engineering challenges the design itself.

cloze.q: ____ sets the direction; ____ designs the solution; ____ implements the technology.
cloze.teach: Start with goals, translate them into design requirements, and then choose actual technology.

cloze.q: Consistent procedures demonstrate ____; connected processes demonstrate ____.
cloze.teach: The same way of working is standardization. Sharing information and coordinating work is integration.

cloze.q: ____ supports a functional area; ____ connects enterprise functions.
cloze.teach: Scope and cross-functional integration distinguish these information systems.

cloze.q: Within one organization is ____; between organizations is ____.
cloze.teach: Intra means within; inter means between. ERP II extends to business partners.
